name: Box64 BOX32 mode: every guest allocation must land below 2^32 because guest pointers are stored in 32 bits
component: Box64 BOX32: 64-byte block allocator, is32bits path (custommem.c)
required_postconditions: Box64 achieves this negatively: reverveHigMem32 first mmaps and holds EVERY free range above 4 GiB, in chunks from 1 TiB down to 64 KiB, so that later unhinted host mmaps have nowhere else to go
the guest address space is therefore defined by what Box64 has NOT reserved, not by any range it requested

failure_sink.description: if a block for 32-bit use comes back above 0xffffffff the allocator clears is32bits, sets errno = ENOMEM and returns NULL. The guest sees an out-of-memory condition rather than a truncated pointer, so the failure is loud but the allocation is simply lost.

source_locations.symbol: if (is32bits && p > (void*)0xffffffffLL) { ... errno = ENOMEM; return NULL; }
reverveHigMem32: uintptr_t cur_size = 1024LL*1024*1024*1024; // start with 1TB check
if((cur==MAP_FAILED) || (cur<(void*)0x100000000LL)) - anything the kernel hands back BELOW 4 GiB is rejected and released, because that space belongs to the guest
PersonalityAddrLimit32Bit() - Box64 additionally asks the kernel for ADDR_LIMIT_32BIT
int isReserved = box64_is32bits && (uintptr_t)addr>0xffffffffLL - freed dynarec memory above 4 GiB is immediately re-reserved so it cannot leak back to the guest

extraction_limitations: size 4096 is a representative guest allocation; the requirement applies to every guest mapping regardless of size.

the real requirement is a bound on the RETURNED address ('< 2^32'), which this schema has no field for. pointer_storage_width_bits=32 is the closest available encoding and is justified by the ENOMEM test at line 843, but it is not the same statement: 32-bit storage would truncate, whereas Box64 detects and refuses.

x_campaign.rationale: An unhinted mmap on x86-64 Linux returns an address near 0x7f.., far above 2^32; without Box64's pre-reservation trick a 32-bit guest pointer slot cannot hold what the host returns.
